---
title: "Stage 7 — compare against what was built"
---

The stage that tells you whether any of it was right.

## What this is

Here, the study already had analysis datasets built by a programmer working from the same plan.
Comparing the executed result against them is the strongest external check available, because
the two implementations are genuinely independent.

**Most readers will not have that, and it is worth being clear about why.** An independently
built implementation exists when someone has already done the work by hand — which is true of a
study being re-examined, and false of one being specified for the first time. On a new study
there is nothing to compare against, and in the world these standards are aiming at there is
nothing to compare against *by design*: the point of a declared specification is to stop having
two implementations that must be reconciled.

So this stage is partly transitional. It is most useful now, while both worlds exist.

**What to do instead, when there is nothing to compare against.** Reproduce the engine's number
outside the engine, using the engine's own selection — the filters and joins its console
reported at stage 6. That is a weaker check than an independent implementation, because it
shares the engine's assumptions, but it is the one that actually found the mechanism described
below: not by disagreeing with the answer, but by making the engine's choices explicit enough to
see.

## What you do

Fit the same model on the study's own derived variables and compare. Where the two disagree,
reproduce the engine's number outside the engine, using the engine's own selection.

## What you should see

Two numbers that do not match, and an explanation of every part of the gap — with each
engine result reproduced to four decimals once its selection is known.

Here they are, for both endpoints, at the current pin. The reference in each case is the same
model fitted on the study's own derived variables — its change, its baseline, its
analysis-record flag — and the count is the subjects on which the engine's baseline row is not
the row the study's flag marks. Every figure is read from the runs.

| Laboratory, ANCOVA at C2D1 | |
|---|---|
| Engine, placebo minus torivumab | {{fact:lab.engine.diff|4}} (SE {{fact:lab.contrast.se|3}}) |
| Reference, same model on the study's variables | {{fact:lab.reference.diff|4}} (SE {{fact:lab.reference.se|3}}) |
| Subjects whose baseline row differs | {{fact:lab.baseline.differ}} of {{fact:lab.baseline.subjects}} |

| Blood pressure, MMRM at C2D1 | |
|---|---|
| Engine, placebo minus torivumab | {{fact:vitals.mmrm.c2d1.estimate|4}} (SE {{fact:vitals.mmrm.c2d1.se|3}}) |
| Reference, same model on the study's variables | {{fact:vitals.mmrm.c2d1.reference|4}} (SE {{fact:vitals.mmrm.c2d1.reference.se|3}}) |
| Subjects whose baseline row differs | {{fact:vitals.baseline.differ}} of {{fact:vitals.baseline.subjects}} |

The second gap is the larger, and for a reason the model makes plain: under a repeated-measures
model the baseline enters every visit's change, not one.

### Step into the factory

The comparisons are `comparison.md` in `endpoints/01-simple-lab-cfb/` and
`endpoints/04-vitals-cfb-mmrm/`, each with the reference fit, the replica of the engine's
selection outside the engine, and the classification of every cause. The subject counts come
from `tools/check_baseline_ambiguity.py`, run against the study's data. The three classes a
divergence is sorted into are set in `docs/specification.md`.

## What to look out for

**A divergence is a result, not a failure, but only if you can explain all of it.** The
mechanism here is a baseline-row disagreement, and it is worth stating as a rule rather than a
symptom. The plan defines baseline *by date*: the last value on or before the first dose. The
chain declared it *by visit*: the record at the Baseline visit. A subject with a screening draw
and a pre-dose draw on day one has two records at that visit, and the two rules pick different
ones — the study's flag marks the later, the engine takes the first it finds. It affects most
subjects in both endpoints.

Explaining all of it means sorting every cause. The comparison record does so into three
classes: an **authoring error**, which the builder could have been made to get right — the
covariate defaulting to the analysis value, the cube on the collected visit rather than the
analysis visit — and was, in the later runs; a **model limitation**, which no authoring fixes —
the chain can state the visit but not which record in it, and nothing produces the
analysis-record flag; and a **specification ambiguity**, of which this endpoint had none, since
the plan was precise. On the data as first pinned, the record substituted the flag's row for
the first row, changed nothing else, and most of the gap closed; what remained was the
analysis-record flag and the visit column, both in the second class. The study's data has been
regenerated since and every number moved — the mechanism did not, which is the point.

Reproduce before you conclude. A gap you cannot reproduce outside the engine is not yet
understood, and the temptation to call it a rounding difference is strong and usually wrong.
